The Undying Revolution
Netaji · The INA · The Rani of Jhansi Regiment
Origins
Subhas Chandra Bose (1897–1945), known reverently as Netaji — "Respected Leader" — was among the most radical and electrifying figures of India's independence movement. Where others sought dialogue, Bose sought armed liberation. After escaping British house arrest in Calcutta in 1941, he traversed Afghanistan, reached Nazi Germany, and ultimately made his way to Imperial Japan — all in pursuit of a single goal: a free India.
The Indian National Army
In 1943, Bose assumed command of the Indian National Army — Azad Hind Fauj — in Southeast Asia. Born from Indian prisoners of war captured after the fall of Singapore and civilian volunteers across Malaya and Burma, the INA under Bose grew to over 85,000 soldiers. Its motto: Ittehad, Etmad, Qurbani — Unity, Faith, Sacrifice.

The INA fought in the Burma Campaign and pressed into Northeast India during the Imphal-Kohima operations of 1944 — briefly planting the Indian tricolour on Indian soil.
The Rani of Jhansi Regiment
Among Bose's most revolutionary acts was the formation of the Rani of Jhansi Regiment — one of the first all-female combat units in Asian military history. Named after warrior-queen Lakshmibai and commanded by Captain Lakshmi Sahgal, the regiment trained in combat, bore arms, and served on active operations. The photograph above shows Netaji personally inspecting this regiment — a moment that defied every colonial and social convention of its era.
Azad Hind Government
On 21 October 1943, Bose declared the Arzi Hukumat-e-Azad Hind — the Provisional Government of Free India — in Singapore. Recognised by nine nations, it declared war on Britain and the United States. Bose's immortal words rang across the subcontinent:

"Tum mujhe khoon do, main tumhe azadi dunga."
"Give me your blood, and I shall give you freedom."
Legacy
Netaji is believed to have died on 18 August 1945 in a plane crash in Taipei — though mystery shrouds the circumstances to this day. When the British tried INA officers at Delhi's Red Fort, the resulting public outrage — cutting across Hindu, Muslim, and Sikh communities — is widely credited as a decisive catalyst that convinced the British Empire that India could no longer be held. The revolution did not die with its leader. It became India.
What is SATYA
Strategic Analysis & Tactical Yield Agency
The Name
Satya — Sanskrit for Truth. In a world of noise, manufactured consent, and engineered confusion, SATYA exists as a counter-force: an agency dedicated to cutting through to what is real, what is strategic, and what endures.
The Mission
SATYA is a strategic intelligence and analysis collective, progressing through five establishments toward full initiation on 08 February 2032. Until then, the agency operates in silent preparation — building frameworks, archiving knowledge, and sharpening the instruments of clarity.
The Philosophy
Inspired by the legacy of those who refused to accept the world as it was handed to them — SATYA draws from the tradition of radical clarity, disciplined sacrifice, and long-horizon thinking. We do not react. We analyse. We do not follow. We yield results.
